claims.text: The baseline alloy forms a thin, protective oxide film during high-temperature exposure.
Interphase boundaries between dissimilar phases develop weakly adherent oxide films.
Mechanical wear preferentially removes incipient oxide films at interphase boundaries.
Removal of the oxide film exposes fresh heterogeneous metallic surfaces.
Compositional differences between the alloy phases establish local galvanic couples when wear exposes them.
Local galvanic coupling accelerates localized corrosion of the exposed surfaces.
Localized corrosion reduces material integrity and wear resistance.
Oxide removal, galvanically enhanced corrosion, and corrosion-assisted wear form a positive feedback loop.
The feedback loop causes total degradation to exceed the sum of degradation from wear-only and corrosion-only exposure.
Approximately 350°C is sufficient to promote active or rapid oxidation in this alloy under the proposed test conditions.
Chloride ions can exploit wear-induced exposure of fresh metal and promote localized corrosion.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion will produce deeper wear tracks than the matched wear-only response.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion will produce a higher density of corrosion pits than the matched corrosion-only response.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion will produce mass loss greater than the sum of mass losses from matched wear-only and corrosion-only tests.
A robust, adherent protective oxide would suppress or eliminate the proposed coupled degradation mechanism.
Low environmental corrosivity would suppress or eliminate the proposed coupled degradation mechanism.
Maintaining oxide integrity with a protective coating should reduce the synergistic degradation response.
Parallel simultaneous, wear-only, corrosion-only, and inert or inhibited tests at matched temperature and duration constitute the proposed controlled comparison.
